title: Possible {name} in source
description: The file contains {name}. Key material in source lets anyone with read access derive the same signatures or decrypt the same data until the key is retired. Shape-only: the match does not prove the key is live.
remediation: Retire the key, re-issue it with the narrowest scope that still works, and load the replacement from a KMS or secret manager rather than from the repository.
limitation: Shape-only: a 16+ character base64 or hex literal assigned to a key-material name. It cannot distinguish a working key from a rotated or test key.
fp: Test fixtures and documentation examples that use the same key name with placeholder bodies are the common false positives; the rule vetoes EXAMPLE text and requires 16+ characters with a digit.
recordDesc: {name} in source is key material, not a password: whoever reads it can reproduce every signature, token or ciphertext the key authorises. Retiring the key is the only remediation that survives the exposure.
applicability: Source, configuration, IaC variables and CI files that may embed {name}.
risk: Forged signatures, decryptable data or an impersonated service identity for as long as the key is trusted; HIGH severity.
why: {name} committed to the repository hands the key material to every reader, and key material does not expire on its own.
fix: Retire the exposed key and record the retirement date.
Re-issue a replacement with the narrowest scope that still works.
Load the replacement from a KMS or secret manager at run time.
verifyT: The retired key no longer verifies or decrypts, and no 16+ character literal remains at this name.
